Subject: Dedicated capacity inquiry — commits, billing cadence, and PO process

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Archimedes is seriously considering Redwood Dedicated for inference of our summarization and search models. Before we move to a formal procurement path, finance asked for a clear breakdown of:

- GPU pool sizing guidance for our workload (we're currently averaging ~120B tokens/day, burst to ~220B on business days).
- Throughput guarantees / latency SLOs for reserved pools (what's guaranteed vs best-effort).
- Pricing for reserved commits: monthly vs annual prepay (what discounts apply, and any minimums).
- How true-ups work if actual usage exceeds the commit for a period (proration, billing cadence).
- PO acceptance, invoice cadence (monthly vs annual), and whether you can sign Net 45 payment terms.

If you can send a short pricing sheet and an example invoice cadence we can share with procurement, that would be helpful.

Also attaching our standard PO template (see attachment).

Thanks,
Emma Jensen
Head of Platform Engineering
Archimedes AI

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry — commits, billing cadence, and PO process

Hi Emma — great to hear and thanks for the clear list. I put together a compact options table that maps your expected load to a recommended GPU pool and the typical pricing/contracting options. Summary here (full sheet attached):

Options (baseline sizing for 120B tokens/day):
- Baseline: 4 x A100-like GPUs (steady-state), supports ~18–22M tokens/hour each depending on model family; expected tail-latency SLA: P95 < 220ms.
- Scale target (to cover 220B burst days): 10 x GPUs with burst autoscaling policy; burst billed differently (see below).

Pricing & commits:
- Monthly reserved commit: $72,000 / month for baseline (4 GPU pool). No prepay discount.
- Annual prepay (12 months upfront): $760,000 total (≈12% discount vs 12x monthly). Requires 12-month commitment on baseline pool.
- Enterprise reserved (24+ months or larger pool): custom pricing, additional discounts available.

True-ups and burst:
- True-up cadence: quarterly by default (can do monthly for larger deals). If actual usage > commit over the quarter, we invoice the overage at blended committed rate + overage uplift (list rate). Proration applies for mid-cycle upgrades.
- Burst beyond commit: charged at list on a pay-as-you-go basis; we can add a capped burst allowance (e.g., up to 20% of commit/month) at a negotiated uplift.

Billing & PO/terms:
- Invoices: monthly invoices by default (shows monthly breakdown and quarterly true-up when applicable).
- We accept POs referencing our SOW and deal id. Standard terms are Net 30, but we can request Net 45 for enterprise customers subject to finance approval.

I've attached a pricing spreadsheet and an example monthly invoice template. If you'd like, I can loop in our finance ops to discuss Net 45 and the PO flow with your procurement team.

Next steps: can you confirm whether Archimedes is comfortable with a 12-month prepay, and whether procurement requires Net 45 in the SOW/PO? If so, I'll start the internal approval.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Grace — looping you both in for confirmation on a couple of items for Archimedes (see thread below). Key asks: Net 45 request and annual prepay refund/true-up logic. Details:

- Customer would like Net 45. Is that acceptable for a first-year enterprise ARR of ~760k?
- For annual prepay: do we offer proration/refund if customer downsizes mid-term, or do we require SOW amendment and crediting against future invoices?
- Invoice granularity: procurement needs a single overage invoice per quarter or individual monthly line items (they prefer monthly line-item granularity).

My initial thought: allow Net 45 for deals >= $500k ARR, offer quarterly true-up invoice but include line-item monthly breakdown in the invoice PDF (meets AP needs). For prepay downgrades we can do crediting toward future invoices rather than cash refunds — avoids accounting churn. But want finance confirmation.

Thanks — R

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-04T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity inquiry — Archimedes (Net 45 / annual prepay questions)

Rishi / Marissa — finance here. Quick answers:

- Net terms: Standard Net 30. We can approve Net 45 on a case-by-case basis for deals > $250k ARR; Archimedes' expected ARR (~$760k for annual prepay) meets that threshold. Approve Net 45.

- Annual prepay downgrades: we do not issue cash refunds for mid-term downgrades. We can issue pro-rated credit that flows against future invoices or extend the term of the remaining prepay value (customer choice). For enterprise SOWs we include a downgrade workflow: SOW amendment + credit ledger entry.

- True-up invoicing: We will generate a single true-up invoice per quarter, but the PDF invoice will include monthly line items and a per-month breakout (meets Archimedes AP requirement).

- PO acceptance: we accept POs that reference the SOW and include the Redwood deal id. Please ensure procurement sends the PO to billing@redwood.com and cc the AE.

- Burst billing: charged at list; if you want to include a capped burst allowance (e.g., 20% of commit/month), legal needs that in the SOW as an addendum.

I'll draft a short memo for the AE template that outlines these positions so procurement has clarity.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Finance Ops
Redwood Inference

Emma — thanks for the patience. Following internal sign-off here is the agreed approach and next steps so procurement has a clean set of bullets to action: 

Summary of agreed commercial terms:
- Sizing: baseline 4x GPUs (handles ~120B tokens/day). We will provision burst autoscaling up to 10 GPUs for peak usage; burst is billable at list rate but we will include a capped burst allowance of 20% of monthly commit for the first 6 months.
- Pricing: annual prepay (12 months) at $760,000 total (~12% discount vs monthly), or monthly reserved commits at $72,000/month with no prepay discount.
- True-up: quarterly true-up invoice for any overages; invoice PDF will include month-by-month line items for AP reconciliation.
- Downgrades/refunds: no cash refunds for mid-term downgrades; we will issue pro-rated credits against future invoices or amend the SOW to extend remaining value (customer choice).
- PO & invoices: we accept POs referencing the SOW + deal id (D-2026-041). Send POs to billing@redwood.com. Invoices will be issued monthly.
- Net terms: Net 45 approved for this deal.

Attachments included: redwood_dedicated_pricing_v2.xlsx (pricing breakdown) and a sample invoice PDF. I've also attached our copy of the PO template for reference.

Next steps (action owners):
